VS.

full_judgment:
2. Md. Abdul Halim Miah obtained an ex parte decree on 12.8.59 in OC Suit No. 15 of 1959 from the 2nd Court of Munsif, Pabna. He instituted OC Execution Case No. 3 of 1962 which was dismissed for default on 2.5.63. Four other Execution Cases, namely, OC Execution Case Nos. 9/62, 3/63, 5/66 and 15/67 were filed by him. but all of them were dismissed for default, the last Execution Case having been filed on 27.12.67 and having been dismissed for default on 6.4.68. Respondent Abdul Mannan, a son of the decree-holder Md. Abdul Halim Miah, as the next friend of his father, filed another OC Execution Case No. 5 of 1977 on 26.8.77 with a petition for condonation of delay under sections 5 and 6 of the Limitation Act on the ground that the decree-holder could not proceed with the earlier Execution Cases owing to his insanity. 

 3. The present appellant filed an objection under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure whereupon Miscellaneous Case No. 38 of 1978 was started. 

 4. The appellant's objections were that the decree-holder was not an insane person and that his son Abdul Mannan has no legal right to represent him as his next friend and that the execution case was barred by limitation as it was not filed within 3 "years of dismissal of OC Execution Case No. 15 of1967 on 6.4.68. The appellant's further case was that the judgment-debtors Gour Gopal Saha and others left for India before the 6th September, 1965 and the suit property was treated as vested property.The decree-holder at first prayed for release of the suit property but ultimately gave up his prayer and Look lease of the structures standing on the suit plot in the name of his wife. Ameda Khatun with effect from 3.12.65 When the appellant issued notice upon Ameda Khatun directing her to deposit the arrear lease money the decree-holder, his son and wife collusively filed the present Execution case. 

 5. The learned Munsif dismissed the appellant's objections under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 31.1.79 on the finding that the decree-holder was insane since 1968 and that there were no defects or laches in the present Execution Case. The appellant preferred an appeal. Miscellaneous Appeal No. 7 of 1979, which was allowed by the learned Subordinate Judge. Pabna by judgment and order dated 17.12.79 and the case was remanded to the Executing Court to determine the date from which the decree-holder went mad on the finding that there was no basis in its finding that the decree-holder was insane since 1968 as no witness was examined to prove this fact. On remand the learned Munsif again dismissed Miscellaneous Case No. 38 of 1978 on 5.12.80. The appellant again took an appeal, Miscellaneous Appeal No. 120 of 1980 and the 1st Court of Additional District Judge, Pabna by judgment and order dated 8.8.81 allowed the appeal and again sent back the Miscellaneous Case on remand to the Executing Court for a decision as to whether the objector-appellant was a representative of the judgment-debtors. The learned Munsif again dismissed the Miscellaneous Case on 8.12.83 holding that the decree-holder was insane at the time of the judgment. On a further appeal by the objector-appellant. Miscellaneous Appeal No. 28 of 1983, the learned Additional District Judge, Pabna dismissed the appeal holding that the decree-holder had gone mad before the expiry of the period of limitation of 12 years from the date of decree dated 12.8.59 and that the period of insanity was rightly condoned by the Executing Court under sections 5 and 6 of the Limitation Act. 

 6. The High Court Division in revision refused to interfere in the matter after holding that since disability of the decree-holder continued with the fresh execution proceeding started by decree-holder's son Abdul Mannan the finding of the Courts below regarding condonation of delay cannot be questioned" and that "section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure has no manner of application in this case" and that "OC Execution Case No. 5 of 1977 though filed after expiration of 3 years from the date passed in Execution Case No. 15 of 1967, it cannot be said that execution case is hit by limitation". 

 7. Leave was granted to consider the appellant's submission that the High Court Division erred in law in holding that section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure has no manner of application in this case inasmuch as section 48 CPC prescribed the maximum period within which the last execution case is to be instituted. 

 10. As already observed the decree-holder obtained the decree in OC Suit No.15 of 1959 on 12.8.59 and the decree-holder's son Abdul Mannan as his next friend filed the latest Execution Case NO.5 of 1977 on 26.8.77 with an application for condonation of delay under sections 5 and 6 of the Limitation Act. Clearly therefore the decree-holder's next friend filed the last Execution Case more than 18 years after the decree was obtained. 

 11. In support of his submission that the last Execution Case was barred by section 48 CPC Mr. Moksudur Rahman has relied upon some decisions ail of which are not relevant. This Court has, however, already pronounced itself on this point in the case of Bangladesh Jatiya Samabaya Bank Ltd. vs. Sangbad Daily Paper and others, BCR 1983 (AD) 418. The said decision was given on consideration of the cases of Md. Abdur Rahim and others vs. Sree Sree Gredhari Jeo. 27 DLR (Dhaka) 72. Pingle Venkata Rama Reddy vs. Kakaria Buchanna and others. AIR 1963 Andhra Pradesh (FB) 1 and Lalji Raja and Sons vs. Firm Hansraj Nathuram, AIR 1971 (SC) 974. This Court approved of the approach of the then Dhaka High Court in the afore-cited cases in 27 DLR (Dhaka) 72 and affirmed that both section 48 CPC and Article 182(2) of the First Schedule to the Limitation Act provide the period of limitation for the execution of a decree. The Civil Procedure Code fixes the longest period whereas the Limitation Act fixes the earliest period to take the first step in execution and the subsequent steps known as steps-in-aid. This Court also affirmed the further view of the then Dhaka High Court that an application for execution has therefore to satisfy first Article 182 of the Limitation Act being the earliest period prescribed and then also section 48 CPC which prescribed the maximum period of limitation. If the execution petition is hit by any of the two provisions it is to fail. 

 13. We therefore accept the submission of Mr. Moksudur Rahman that the latest Execution Case No. 5 of 1977 filed on 26.8.77 is barred by section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure and that the High Court Division erred in law in holding that section 48 CPC has no manner of application in this case. 

 The appeal is allowed without any order as to costs. Miscellaneous case No. 38 of 1978 is allowed and the respondent's Execution Case No. 5 of 1977 is dismissed as being barred under section 48 CPC.
